title: Continuous Quantum Feedback Control via Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Quantum feedback control requires acting on noisy continuous measurement records without direct access to the underlying quantum state. We propose Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning, a pipeline in which a recurrent encoder, constrained to the Stiefel manifold, produces density-matrix estimates that are guaranteed positive-semidefinite and trace-normalized by construction, embedding quantum state geometry directly into the learning loop. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) actor then maps these physically valid belief states to continuous control actions. On a simulated continuously monitored qubit, the resulting policy achieves stable feedback control, maintaining a measurement-conditioned belief fidelity of approximately 0.77-0.80 and exhibiting substantially lower return variance than a parameter-matched LSTM-history baseline across both nominal and out-of-distribution conditions. Although gains in raw target fidelity are modest, the geometric constraint guarantees a physically valid, interpretable belief representation and yields markedly more stable control under measurement inefficiency and abrupt dynamics switches. These results indicate that physics-informed neural memory is a practical inductive bias for reliable quantum feedback control.
summary: The paper introduces Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning for controlling open quantum systems based only on noisy measurements. By constraining the learned belief state ($\hat{ho}_t$) to maintain physical validity (PSD and trace normalization), the method ensures reliable control policies. This approach proves more stable than standard deep learning baselines, particularly when system dynamics change unexpectedly.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving continuous quantum feedback control when only noisy measurement records are available, without direct access to the true underlying quantum state.
main_result: The proposed Kraus-Belief PPO method achieves stable feedback control with significantly lower return variance than unconstrained baselines, especially under out-of-distribution conditions.
method: It uses a two-stage pipeline: a Kraus-constrained recurrent encoder estimates the density matrix ($\hat{ho}_t$), which is then fed into a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) actor for action selection.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a continuously monitored open quantum qubit, whose dynamics are governed by a stochastic master equation. Control involves applying a continuous scalar field $u_t$ to steer the state towards a target pure state $ho^\star$.
key_observables: Measurement-conditioned belief fidelity ($\sim 0.77–0.80$), return variance, mean episodic return, and physical validity metrics (PSD check, trace error).
important_parameters: Control action bounds ($u_t \in [-4, 4]$), measurement efficiency ($\eta$), and the PPO hyperparameters.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that enforcing physics-informed neural memory via the Kraus constraint acts as a practical inductive bias for reliable quantum feedback control.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the comparison between the Kraus-belief PPO pipeline and the LSTM baseline, highlighting how the Stiefel manifold projection enforces physical state constraints.
paper_structure: The paper defines the problem in terms of a POMDP, proposes the two-stage Kraus-Belief PPO method (encoder pretraining followed by RL control), compares it against an unconstrained LSTM baseline across nominal and OOD conditions, and analyzes performance metrics like variance stability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical implementation gap in quantum control theory by embedding fundamental physical constraints (like PSD) into the learning architecture, making RL policies applicable to real-world open quantum systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Kraus-belief PPO pipeline. The observation history ht passes through a frozen pretrained Kraus encoder (via a Stiefel manifold projection) to produce a physically valid density-matrix belief ˆρt. Explicit physical features ϕt are then passed to the PPO actor. The LSTM baseline replaces this entire belief stage with a plain recurrent encoder.
